subject: Packaging negotiation: staggered credits for Optimize Toolkit pilot
body:
From: Elena Park <elena@lighthouse.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@lighthouse.ai>
Date: Mon, 29 Nov 2027 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Pilot pricing and technical scope questions

Hi Hannah —

Thanks again for the demo last week. We talked internally and want to scope a 3-month pilot for the Optimize Toolkit focused on:
- batching/caching guidance for our conversational inference workload (p95 latency target ~120ms)
- quantization recommendations (we're evaluating int8 vs int4 for accuracy tradeoffs)
- a modest commitment so we can evaluate unit economics before expanding

Budget constraints mean we prefer credits/offsets rather than a large upfront cash commit. Can Redwood propose a packaging that balances:
1) an initial credit tranche to cover P0 testing,
2) milestone-linked credits to de-risk the trial, and
3) a path to convert usage into a committed annual band if the pilot looks good.

Two practical asks from our side:
- Can you include expected token-cost savings projections with batching + KV cache assumptions?
- Any guardrails you recommend if quantization degrades generation quality?

Appreciate a sketch we can present to procurement.

Best,
Elena Park
Head of AI Product
Lighthouse AI

On Mon, Nov 29, 2027 at 17:05 Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com> wrote:

Date: Mon, 29 Nov 2027 17:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Pilot pricing and technical scope questions

Elena — great to hear you're moving forward. Attached is a short term sheet (Optimize_Pilot_Term_Sheet.pdf) that sketches a staggered-credit model which we've used successfully with other mid-market pilots. High-level proposal: 

- Upfront: 60% credit tranche (applied to tokens/embeddings) to cover integration and initial testing window.
- Milestone: 30% released on successful completion of two acceptance gates (integration tests pass; quality regressions within agreed thresholds).
- Conversion reserve: 10% retained to offset first-month post-conversion overages if you decide to convert to a 12-month committed band.

Why staggered credits: it keeps your procurement exposure low while giving our team runway to tune batching/caching and recommended quant settings. For your p95 target, we expect batching improvements to reduce cost-per-token by ~20-35% depending on traffic shape; KV cache can further reduce repeated-prefix costs by another 10-25% for dialog use cases. I'll call those out more precisely in Rafael's note below.

Quantization: Rafael and infra will propose a safe path — start with symmetric int8 for embeddings and generation, run a small eval set to check top-line metrics, and then consider an experimental int4 bucket for non-critical inference paths if accuracy holds. We recommend running the eval in parallel to the pilot and gating any int4 rollout on an agreed quality delta (e.g., <1.5% BLEU-equivalent drop or equivalent task metric).

Next steps: Rafael, can you confirm expected latency/throughput tradeoffs and a short checklist for acceptance gates? Laura, want to align on commercial constraints (SOW, payment timing, SLA credits). Connor, could you handle a quick HubSpot update for DL-8452 and share the link?

Thanks — short call tomorrow to walk the term sheet? Happy to host.

Regards,
Hannah Schmitt
Senior Sales Manager | Redwood Inference

Elena / team — quick technical addendum from infra:

1) Latency and batching: For a p95 ~120ms target on 8k-context-ish requests we recommend using adaptive batching with a 20ms short-window cutoff (to avoid high tail latency). Expect 15-30% CPU/GPU utilization uplift during batching peaks; batching wins are larger when request size distribution is heavily right-skewed.

2) KV caching: If your dialogs have repeated prefixes (retrieval-augmented or chained prompts), a warmed KV cache can yield 10-30% token reduction on typical sessions. Plan for a cache-warmup window (48-72 hours) during the pilot and instrument cache-hit metrics in the acceptance gates.

3) Quantization path: Start with per-channel symmetric int8 on weights + quant-aware coupling for attention kernels. Accuracy regressions are usually modest; however:
   - Measure generation quality on your eval set (we recommend 1k prompt pairs covering critical intents).
   - If you consider int4, do it behind a canary variant and only for high-volume, low-sensitivity routes. Rollback should be automated if distortion metrics exceed the threshold.

4) Failure/rollback guardrails: Add a safety cutoff that automatically routes to a full-precision variant if latency > 4x baseline or if quality metrics dip below agreed thresholds.

I've attached a short workbook with conservative cost-savings scenarios (quant-recs.xlsx). The workbook models varying cache-hit rates and quant bands (int8/int4) against throughput and expected token cost.

Happy to jump on a 20-minute call to walk the workbook with your infra folks.

Cheers,
Rafael Mendes
Director, Inference Engineering | Redwood Inference
rafael_mendes@redwood.com

Elena / team — from a commercial ops perspective, the staggered-credit model is acceptable for a three-month pilot. A few clarifications: 

- Payment and SOW: We can issue a short SOW that references the term sheet. Payment will be via credit note applied to your account; procurement will want the standard net-30 on any cash components.
- SLA credits: we don't typically tie SLA credits to pilot credit release, but we can include a limited uptime target and a credit schedule if that helps procurement sign off.
- Conversion to committed band: to convert the pilot into a 12-month committed contract, we need a written notice 14 days before pilot end and a minimum 3x baseline usage commitment to qualify for the highest discount band.

If the above looks reasonable, Hannah / Connor — can you share a draft SOW and a HubSpot record? Elena, we'll also need a short statement of intent from procurement for the staggered credits.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
